task.problem: Cross-project audit of AIOS-renew and Python Agent failure history exposed a remaining control-plane blind spot. TASK-047 correctly transports bounded ADMISSION_FAILURE diagnostics for REMEDIATION after repository/TASK resolution, but explicitly excluded PRIMARY, REPAIR, direct-candidate acceptance, and other Operator surfaces. Current PRIMARY synchronization under TASK-062 can reject dirty, detached, ahead, diverged, missing/ambiguous-upstream, fetch, fast-forward, stale-kernel, or RUN-namespace state before a RUN exists. TASK-077 records that downstream historical REPAIR attempts can fail during remote lineage/snapshot admission with no RUN at all. TASK-071 recovery admission and TASK-078 historical REMEDIATION subject admission likewise have valid fail-closed pre-RUN boundaries. Those failures can currently exist only as terminal/UI text unless they happen to pass through TASK-047's REMEDIATION wrapper. In addition, historical admission diagnostics such as the observed Python Agent TASK-166/F1R1 case record an error string but not the exact remediation-ref commit/snapshot identity seen when the failure occurred; if that remote ref later changes, forensic review cannot prove what immutable state the resolver actually observed. This is an observability and attribution defect, not authority to weaken admission, retry Git/model operations, or create repairable fake RUNs.
